title: The Great Pumpkin String Mix-Up
markdown:
Mr. Moss adored his pumpkins. Every morning he grabbed his sunshine-yellow string to measure them. Bartholomew, his biggest pumpkin, was getting huge.

From the garden fence, Pia the penguin and Rory the red panda peeked. They loved Mr. Moss and his pumpkins. But oh, how they loved those mischievous ducks — especially Dabble, their leader. The ducks adored that bright yellow string. They'd tug it, peck it, tote it like a prize.

"Look, Rory!" Pia chirped, wings flapping. "The ducks are playing with the string again!"

Rory giggled. "They think it's a wiggly yellow dragon!"

Mr. Moss just sighed. "Oh, bother." The string was for Bartholomew's measurements. Each day he'd find it tangled, stretched, or used as a duckling slide. Dashing, diving, quacking.

The string was for measuring, not bouncing.

Until one day Bartholomew grew too big for his spot. He bulged against the patch's edge. Mr. Moss's eyebrows knitted. "He needs more room! And the ducks tied my string to the big oak!" It stretched taut, like a giant trampoline.

A tickle of panic. He'd rush out only to find the string bouncing with delighted ducks. Pia and Rory tried to help.

"Perhaps," Pia suggested, "we can show them the string is for growing, not bouncing?"

The ducks quacked louder. Rory tried a shiny pebble; Dabble batted it away and plunged the flock back into the game.

"This is a pickle," Mr. Moss grumbled, watching Bartholomew bulge. The pumpkin was getting squished. The ducks kept bouncing, quacking with pure joy, unaware of the predicament.

Pia and Rory put their heads together. "Aha!" They gathered sparkly leaves, smooth pebbles, fluffy feathers. They made a dazzling trail away from the patch toward a sunny clearing. Pia nudged the yellow string. Rory gave it a gentle tug. They dragged the glistening string along the glittering path.

The ducks spotted the moving string. Beady eyes widened. Dabble honked a mighty excited honk. They looked at Bartholomew, then at the beckoning string. The biggest, most spectacular game was on offer. Happy quacks, delighted splashes, the flock dashed after it, following the trail. Pia and Rory giggled, guiding them to the clearing. There, with a triumphant honk from Dabble, they showed the ducks a different, thicker rope for a super-duper tug-of-war.

Mr. Moss dashed to Bartholomew. He untangled the yellow string, damp but intact, and quickly measured his magnificent pumpkin.

"He has room to grow!" A wide grin. He watched, charmed, as ducks, penguin, and panda cheered their jolly tug-of-war. The sparkly trail had made the perfect distraction.

Ever since, the pumpkins grew plump in their spacious patch, and the ducks had a rope of their own. Pia did not declare the day amazing to the sky. She wondered, with a happy squeak, whether Bartholomew would need an even longer string by next week — and whether Dabble would try to borrow that one too, dragon or no dragon.

The string was for measuring. The rope was for bouncing. And that, Mr. Moss thought, stretching the yellow line along a pumpkin the size of a small moon, was a much tidier sort of bother.
